_comment: The way UP (plan-underworld.md U3): CaveMouth's twin, standing at a passage's lower end. Every knob is cave-mouth.json's — see that file's comment for why the body recipe is what it is, why the art is a placeholder Signpost, and why NEITHER file authors a destination (U3b: the placement names its anchor, so one definition serves every upward passage). ⚑ IT IS A SEPARATE DEFINITION FOR ITS WORDS, NOT ITS DESTINATION. Since U3b the destination is per placement, so a second file buys only the text and the lines — 'a narrow shaft with daylight at the top' is not a thing you can say with the downward door's words. If a passage ever wants the same words at both ends, one definition placed twice is now enough. ⚑ The pairing is CONTENT, not structure: nothing links these two files, and nothing checks that a zone placing one also places the other. A one-way drop is legal and may well be the point somewhere. ⛔ The campfire-dwell trap (plan-portal-spells.md D8) applies to this end too, and it is the likelier of the two to be violated: an exit is exactly where a cave's campfire wants to stand.
name: CaveExit

lines: A narrow shaft, and daylight at the top of it.

grants.line: You climb back into the light.
